items.title: Stuart Bergen Interview, 1970-07-18
items.q: Yeah, well I remember then hearing you when you first were using Donald Sewer.

ctx.x: Doc Souchon made the presentation. Bill Eastwood was playing banjo at that time. He played with a lot of the old time jazz guys too. But that's about the whole thing in a nutshell as far as that parade and the baseball game and the jazz presentation. But after that I lost those men. They were good musicians, they had a good band, but you can't keep a good man down. When I lose a man I say good luck to you, may you make money, and I start breaking into somebody else if I can't.

Yeah, well I remember then hearing you when you first were using Donald Sewer. Yeah. I guess right after that, sometime along in there. At some place, where was it? Was it back on Hagen Avenue? That's a lot of back. It was a little bit of speakeasy.

And I'll never forget you boys were recording my band and we had the recorder set up in the middle of the floor and some girl that Dutch knew, she got mad. She raised the devil because we were right in the middle of the floor without recording apparatus, but they didn't have anybody in there hardly. I don't see why we were offending them. Maybe they figured somebody might come in and want to dance and think they were not operating. But that piano was so badly out of tune Dick, it wasn't too good. And I think they…
